entries.claim: Task 2's repo-side Verify changes `flags: m` to `flags: ms` in `evals/full-walk/graders/at-most-five-ids.md`. That file is one of the size grader's three byte-held copies, so Task 1's equal-copy check fails on the change by itself, and the step cannot show that the D-09 form check runs over the table's real files.
entries.failure_scenario: Suppose the executor wires the form checker only to the planted patterns and never applies it to the full-grader table's files, which the D-08/must-be-true #4 outcome requires. The mutation still turns the suite red, because the three at-most-five-ids.md copies now differ by bytes (the size check is unaffected, since the pattern holds no `.`). Verify passes even though a full grader carrying `flags: ms`, or any refused form, in a file outside a byte-held set (every-requirement-once.md, every-requirement-traced.md, the recommendation graders) would pass the suite undetected. Mutating a file that is not byte-held, such as evals/epics-from-spine/graders/every-requirement-once.md, would isolate the form check.

entries.claim: Task 1 says `claude plugin eval --help` lists `--case` as the only name filter and `--eval-dir` as the only other flag that changes which cases run. That is false. The help for the installed CLI also lists `--tag <tag...>  Filter cases by tag (repeatable)`, so the test as planned does not deliver AC5's "`--case` or any other case filter" (roadmap criterion 3). The must-be-true at line 19 and the planted inputs at line 40 repeat the same two flags and leave `--tag` out.
entries.failure_scenario: Someone edits README.md's fenced command to `claude plugin eval . --tag smoke --trust-plugin --no-publish ...`. The planned test looks only for `--case`, `--case=` and `--eval-dir`, so it passes: one command line and 58 bullets matching 58 folders. The documented suite command now runs only the tagged subset, which is the coverage failure criterion 3 says the unit test must catch. No planted input exercises `--tag`, so nothing in Verify shows the gap. The same help text says `--max-cost-usd` aborts the run and reports partial results, so a README command with a ceiling would also stop short of every case, and the plan's list of flags that change which cases run doesn't account for it either.

entries.claim: Task 1 has SKILL.md keep allowing the `/seldon architecture` sentence on a line of its own, but readiness-fix's and readiness-fix-answer's unchanged ends-on-confirm.md need the command on the question's own line. Must-be-true 4, that those cases score 1.00, then depends on which form the model happens to pick.

Task 2 says samples/spine-rerun/prd.md is the PRD the go-ahead produces, but nothing checks the fresh capture's Edit inputs against that seed. The history's line 4 (the capture's last message) could then describe a PRD the stale-spine seed does not hold, and Verify wouldn't catch it.
entries.failure_scenario: I rebuilt samples/prd.md from the Edit inputs in the phase 8 kept capture (evals/results/phase-8-traces/full-run-3/prd-conflict-apply.trace.jsonl), and the result matches samples/spine-rerun/prd.md byte for byte. That proves only that one capture matched. The same capture's last message also offers to remove the User journeys reminder sentence. A fresh capture that removes or rewords that sentence on its own would describe it in line 4, while stale-spine's seed.sh still copies the unchanged samples/spine-rerun/prd.md. The replayed history would then contradict the seeded file, against D-17/D-28's rule that the history be one the skill at HEAD produces. Task 2's Verify checks only the line text, the check line, the closing `?`, the session ids and the scores. It never compares the capture's written prd.md with samples/spine-rerun/prd.md, even though D-10 names that rebuild technique for this kind of check.
